root_idea.summary: The root centers on the inward or inner-facing part of a thing, especially the belly as opposed to the back or outward side.
root_idea.development: From the bodily belly and interior, the vocabulary extends to hidden or inward states, inner linings, intimate associates, interiors of places, and related senses of enclosure or centrality.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form I verb with its own concealed or hidden usage.
Quran-attested active-participial noun with distinct inward and divine-epithet usages.
Feminine inflection of the same active participle بَاطِنٌ.
Core Quran-attested noun meaning belly, womb in gestational contexts, and interior.
Distinct noun with Quranic lining and intimate-associate usages.

senses.definition: To be hidden, concealed, or unapparent.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, it occurs in contrast with what is apparent or manifest; this is an intransitive Form I usage.

senses.definition: Inward, inner, hidden, or not outwardly apparent; an interior aspect or part.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran applies this active participle to what is concealed or inward, including an interior part or hidden aspect, in contrast with the apparent or outward.

senses.definition: The Unapparent: a divine epithet denoting the One who knows hidden realities and is beyond being encompassed by perception.
senses.usage_conditions: This specialized epithet occurs in the coordinated divine names in 57:3; it is not merely an ordinary adjective for a concealed object.

senses.definition: Belly or abdomen; the bodily interior of a person or animal.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the ordinary bodily sense in Quranic references to what is inside people or animals, including food, drink, or other contents.

senses.definition: Womb, as the bodily interior in which offspring develop.
senses.usage_conditions: The womb sense is attested in Quranic expressions about embryos, offspring, or human formation within the bellies of mothers.

senses.definition: The interior or inner part of a place or thing.
senses.usage_conditions: In 48:24, بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ refers to the interior of Makkah; this is a place-interior construction rather than a reference to a bodily abdomen.

senses.definition: The lining or inner covering of a garment or other covering.
senses.usage_conditions: In 55:54, the plural refers to the inner linings of the couches or furnishings described there.

senses.definition: A trusted intimate or confidant admitted to a person's private affairs.
senses.usage_conditions: In 3:118, the word is used metaphorically from a garment's lining for an associate who is brought close and knows one's inward affairs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become large or distended in the belly through abundant eating; to become replete.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Classical Form I bodily condition, distinct from the Quranic intransitive sense of being hidden.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exult and behave insolently or ungratefully, especially from satiety or abundance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative development associated with repletion and prosperity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffer a complaint, disease, or pain in the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Passive or patient-oriented bodily usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike or beat someone's belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive Form I usage with the belly as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a disease or fever to enter into or affect a person internally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes an illness taking effect within someone, rather than the person becoming hidden.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter or move about within a valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is a valley or comparable tract of land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To penetrate mentally into a matter and know its inward or intrinsic state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form I usage concerning the real circumstances of an affair or story.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become one of someone's special intimates by entering into his affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic association construction expressing close personal involvement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a lining or inner covering onto a garment or piece of cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II causative or transitive usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove or cut the hair from the underside of the beard beneath the chin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized grooming construction concerning the lower side of the beard.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To consult with a companion in order to learn what is in his mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare Form III usage concerning confidential consultation; the transmitted wording of this entry is textually uncertain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fasten a camel's belly-girth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV usage with the belly-girth of a camel as the object or instrument.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To place a sword beneath the waist or against the body's inner side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A literal placement construction, with a possible figurative extension to keeping the sword as a secret companion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take someone as a special intimate or confidential associate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV causative usage equivalent to taking someone as a بِطَانَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill one's belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V bodily usage concerning eating or repletion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach sexually or have sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form V construction; the evidence supports the sexual relation, not a restriction to any particular object class.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move in the middle or midst of herbage, or to go about within it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is vegetation or a grassy tract.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a place to extend far, with one part remote from another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VI usage describing the spatial extent of a place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To assist a she-camel in delivering her young.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited construction specifies repeated assistance in parturition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek to discover what young is in a mare's belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form X usage concerning determining whether an animal is pregnant and what is within its belly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a stallion to cover she-camels so that they conceive, depositing seed in their wombs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reproductive construction involving animals and internal conception.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter or penetrate into an interior, or to have and hold something concealed within.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form X usage may be physical or mental; the concealment sense describes containment within.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In idiomatic constructions, what is in the belly, including excrement; of a woman, to bring forth a child; of a hen, to lay an egg; and, in a childbirth expression, to die in labor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are fixed or elliptical constructions based on the noun's bodily sense, not separate general meanings of every occurrence of بَطْنٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An inner, underside, middle, or lower part, including the palm of the hand, sole of the foot, underside of a hoof, inner half of a feather, or foundation of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These specialized applications contrast with the outward or upper side; they remain Classical extensions distinct from the Quranic place-interior usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low, depressed, soft, or water-retaining tract of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A landscape term, often contrasted with ظَهْرٌ for higher or outward ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tribal subdivision below a قَبِيلَة, or a comparable intermediate tribal group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A social-structural usage with plural forms أَبْطُنٌ and بُطُونٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease of the belly involving enlargement caused by repletion or related abdominal illness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This noun denotes the condition itself, including the expression for dying from it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person preoccupied with the belly or possessing an inordinate appetite; a voracious eater.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive noun for a belly-centered or excessively food-seeking person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who exults excessively and behaves insolently or ungratefully, especially through abundance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative personal designation related to satiety or wealth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Repletion or the state of being filled with food and drink.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of condition; the proverb associates excessive repletion with diminished intelligence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Exultation that produces insolent and ungrateful behavior; figuratively, prosperity or richness expressed in that manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This includes idiomatic expressions about dying with one's wealth intact or departing in unimpaired religious integrity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The buttocks or posterior part.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun distinct from the ordinary belly meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The roads or beaten tracks running through a valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A pluralized valley expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The belly-girth of a camel or of a saddle, fastened beneath the animal's belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word also occurs in idioms: the meeting of its two rings denotes a severe or straitened affair, while broadness of the girth denotes ease or prosperity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Big or full in the belly; having a large or well-filled abdomen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a person, and also used as a laudatory epithet in one cited description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Full, especially of a purse or provision bags.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited idiom describes concealed travel provisions consumed by their possessor rather than a general restriction on all uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Far-extending.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a long run, distance, or expanse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wide and low or depressed, as a tract of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A landscape adjective combining breadth with low elevation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The second mansion of the Moon, a small triangular group of stars associated with the belly of the Ram.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper astronomical name and diminutive form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A secret or knowledge of the inward state of an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Classical figurative noun sense related to concealment and inner knowledge, distinct from the Quranic intimate-associate construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something placed beneath the main load of a camel, such as a waterskin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical load-bearing construction, especially when paired with عَلَاوَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The inward or intrinsic state of an affair, or the secret thoughts and inner disposition of a person; covertly or secretly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This Classical usage concerns knowledge of hidden circumstances or mental recesses, rather than merely the physical interior of an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A watercourse or place where water flows through rugged ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A landscape noun with plural forms referring to such channels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The middle or retired part of a province, district, or city.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical noun describing an interior administrative or settled area.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vein in the interior of a horse's forearm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical term, also used in the dual for the pair of such veins.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lank or thin in the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person; feminine formation takes the corresponding feminine ending.

other_classical_meanings.definition: White in the back and belly, as applied to a horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equine description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lined or provided with an inner covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial adjective derived from the lining sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One afflicted with a disease or pain of the belly, or one who dies from such an illness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical tradition also treats a person dying from abdominal disease as a martyr.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The apparent, visible part of the sky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression in which بَطْنُ السَّمَاءِ denotes the visible portion of the sky.

cautions: The Form I Quranic verb بَطَنَ is represented in the concealed or hidden sense; its separate Classical bodily, transitive, and inward-knowledge uses are not merged into that Quranic sense.
The rare Form III consultation entry has a textually uncertain transmitted gloss, so its interpretation is retained with that limitation.
The feminine Quranic form بَاطِنَةً is accounted for under the normalized active-participle headword بَاطِنٌ.
